subject: Dedicated pool queueing carveout request — Theta Analytics
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@thetaanalytics.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: procurement <procurement@thetaanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated pool queueing carveout request

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our infra team reviewed Redwood's dedicated offering and we're broadly aligned, but we hit one blocker on the SLA side. Our workload has infrequent but very high tail spikes tied to end-of-quarter batch runs and model refreshes. We need either a guaranteed tail-latency carveout for a reserved GPU pool or a formal burst capacity guarantee with predictable failover rules.

Specifically we're asking for:
- A written exception in the Dedicated SLA for a per-pool 99.9th percentile token latency for bursts up to 60s of sustained traffic.
- An explicit statement about queueing priority (we can't be fully preempted during those windows).
- A clear escalation and credit formula if the carveout isn't respected.

I attached a short note outlining our expected traffic profile (theta-sla-request.pdf). Can the Redwood team confirm whether you can support this as an amendment or if we should size a larger reserved commit?

We're hopeful we can finalize before our procurement window closes on Dec 1. I've cc'd procurement to loop them in.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Operations
Theta Analytics

Attachments: theta-sla-request.pdf
From: logan_wright@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@thetaanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool queueing carveout request

Elena —

Thanks for the clear summary and the traffic profile. Short answer: yes, we can support a carveout, but there are a few ways to structure it and tradeoffs to consider. High level options:

1) Reserved pool + guaranteed headroom: commit N GPUs and we promise an additional burst headroom (example: +30% of commit) for up to X minutes per day across the pool.

2) Priority queue carveout: mark your pool as "burst-protected" so it gets higher queue weight during defined windows; preemption still exists for emergencies but we'll cap preemption to Y nodes.

3) SLA amendment with credits: we can add a 99.9 P99 token latency target for burst windows; if we miss it, we issue credits scaled to minutes of breach.

Marissa / Karthik — adding you for sizing and SLO language.

Elena, can you confirm the following so we can pick the right route:
- Target P95/P99 latency numbers you need (ms)
- Typical burst duration and expected tokens/sec at peak
- Whether you prefer a carveout clause in the base SLA or a one-off addendum for Q4 only

If convenient, let's do a 30-min sync Wednesday (11/17) to lock scope. I'll follow up with a capacity plan (attached) and a proposed amendment template.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity-plan.xlsx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@thetaanalytics.com>, logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool queueing carveout request

Hi Elena —

Quick technical note from our side on queueing behavior and options (so procurement has a sense of impact):

- Queueing model: we run per-pool weighted fair queueing with an emergency preempt path. For a carveout we can escalate your pool weight and place a hard cap on preemption for the reserved pool (e.g., no more than 1 node preempted in a 10-node pool).
- Throughput guarantees: We can guarantee sustained throughput up to the committed GPUs' combined token/sec and specify burst headroom in the SLO. Example wording: "Redwood will provide up to +30% burst capacity above committed baseline for periods not exceeding 90 seconds per burst and not more than 20 minutes per calendar day."
- Tail latency: P99 token latency is driven by batching and KV cache hits; to meet a tight P99 (eg <200ms) we recommend enabling prefix caching and reserving additional KV cache memory in the pool.

Suggested SLO clause (draft):
"For dedicated pools under Deal D-THETA-00912, Redwood will provide a burst headroom of 30% above the committed GPU baseline for bursts no longer than 90 seconds. During defined burst windows, Redwood will increase the pool queue weight for Theta Analytics and will not preempt more than 10% of committed nodes. If Redwood fails to meet the agreed P99 token latency for a qualified burst window, customer will receive service credits proportional to the duration of the breach."

Logan — I've sketched some numbers in the attached capacity-plan.xlsx. Happy to refine after the sync.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@thetaanalytics.com>

Thanks everyone — this reads well and addresses most of our concerns. A few clarifying points from procurement/legal:
- We prefer a one-off amendment for Q4 (through Mar 31) with an option to renew subject to performance.
- The credit formula needs to be concrete — procurement suggested credits equal to 1% of monthly committed fees per 10 minutes of qualified breach, up to 30% of the monthly bill.
- DocuSign workflow: please include Sam Chen from our procurement team (sam.chen@enterprisecloud.co) and I'll route internally.

We'll accept a +30% burst headroom for 90s bursts for Q4 as a starting point, with the clause you proposed as the basis for the amendment. Can you circulate the amendment and a short runbook describing escalation steps?

On the sync, Wednesday works; can we do 11/24 at 10am PT instead (we're in a heavy release window this week)?

Best,
Elena
